Bach: “O Haupt voll Blut und Wunden”

“O Sacred Head, Now Wounded”, analysed by Dmitri Tymoczko

Bach’s chorale “O Haupt voll Blut und Wunden” from the St Matthew Passion, in four parts, with Dmitri Tymoczko’s Roman-numeral analysis under the notes (When in Rome). Play along with the analysis.

From the St Matthew Passion (BWV 244.54; no. 74 in Riemenschneider’s collection of the chorales). Bach harmonized this melody several times; this is one of them. How to read the labels and use the score: Analysed Scores.

Analysis: Dmitri Tymoczko.

The analyst’s notes:

  • please email corrections to dmitri@princeton.edu
  • unusual vi-viio-I progression where leading tone falls in soprano; could read first two chords as i-iv in d.
  • quarter-note suspension in tenor, beat 3
  • the first beat of m7 can be read either as a deceptive cadence to vi6 or as Imaj7 followed by a lower neighbor, or as a combination of these.

Other readings the analyst gives:

  • Bar 1: IV viiø⁴₃ I⁶ ii vii°⁶ I
  • Bar 7: vi⁶ g: i⁶ V⁶₅ i
  • Bar 7: IM⁷ g: i⁶ V⁶₅ i

Things to find

  • The key changes: the phrases end in F, then D minor, then B♭ and G minor, then C and back to F. Each new key is reached through its own dominant, as in Chapter 22.
  • Bar 6: IV⁶₄ over a held F in the bass, then I.
  • Bar 7: IM⁷. The analyst’s notes give other readings: a deceptive cadence to vi⁶, or IM⁷ followed by a lower neighbor.

Gotham, Mark, et al. When in Rome: A Meta-Corpus of Functional Harmony. GitHub. github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome. The analyses on this page (RomanText files), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

Hutchinson, Robert. “Modulation.” Music Theory for the 21st-Century Classroom, ch. 22, U of Puget Sound. musictheory.pugetsound.edu/mt21c/Modulation.html. Tonicization against modulation, closely related keys, diatonic and chromatic pivot chords, and direct, common-tone and sequential modulation.

Sapp, Craig Stuart, encoder. 370 Four-part Chorales by J. S. Bach in the Humdrum File Format. GitHub. github.com/craigsapp/bach-370-chorales. The chorale’s notes (after Dörffel’s edition, Breitkopf & Härtel, c. 1875), converted to ABC for this page.

Tymoczko, Dmitri, analyst. Roman-numeral analyses of the Bach chorales and of Beethoven, Piano Sonata Op. 27 No. 2, in When in Rome. github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome/tree/master/Corpus. The chorale’s analysis; his readings of the Moonlight are quoted where they differ from Chen and Su’s.
